arguments.command:
python -c "
import parse

# Test with a named result
r = parse.parse('{name} is {age}', 'Alice is 30')
print('Result:', r)
print('fixed:', r.fixed)
print('named:', r.named)

# Test key lookup (string should check named dict)
print()
print('Testing __contains__:')
print(\"'name' in r:\", 'name' in r)
print(\"'age' in r:\", 'age' in r)
print(\"'missing' in r:\", 'missing' in r)

# Test value lookup
print()
print(\"'Alice' in r:\", 'Alice' in r)
print(\"'Bob' in r:\", 'Bob' in r)
print(\"30 in r:\", 30 in r)

# Test with fixed results only
r2 = parse.parse('{} is {}', 'Alice is 30')
print()
print('Result without names:', r2)
print('fixed:', r2.fixed)
print('named:', r2.named)
print(\"'Alice' in r2:\", 'Alice' in r2)
print(\"'Bob' in r2:\", 'Bob' in r2)
print(\"30 in r2:\", 30 in r2)
print(\"'name' in r2:\", 'name' in r2)

# Test search
r3 = parse.search('{name}', 'Hello Alice world')
print()
print('Search result:', r3)
print(\"'name' in r3:\", 'name' in r3)
print(\"'Alice' in r3:\", 'Alice' in r3)
"
